syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Importance of chemistry and nature of matter

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how chemistry contributes to health, industry and the environment.
Explain the solid, liquid and gaseous states in terms of particle arrangement and motion.
Classify matter into mixtures, elements and compounds.

topics.title: Properties of matter and their measurement

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the SI base units and the quantities they measure.
Distinguish mass from weight and convert between units of volume.
Calculate density and convert temperatures between the Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales.

topics.title: Uncertainty in measurement

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the rules of significant figures and scientific notation to measured quantities and results.
Distinguish precision from accuracy using sets of measurements.
Convert units using the unit factor method.

topics.title: Laws of chemical combinations

concepts.learning_objective: State the law of conservation of mass and its significance.
Apply the laws of definite and multiple proportions to mass data.
Apply Gay Lussac's law of gaseous volumes and Avogadro's law.

topics.title: Dalton's atomic theory and atomic and molecular masses

concepts.learning_objective: State the postulates of Dalton's atomic theory.
Define the atomic mass unit and calculate average atomic mass from isotopic data.
Calculate molecular mass and explain when formula mass is used.

topics.title: Mole concept, percentage composition and empirical formula

concepts.learning_objective: Relate mass, moles and number of particles using molar mass and the Avogadro constant.
Calculate the mass per cent of an element in a compound.
Derive empirical and molecular formulas from percentage composition and molar mass.

topics.title: Stoichiometry, limiting reagent and reactions in solutions

concepts.learning_objective: Use a balanced equation to calculate masses of reactants and products.
Identify the limiting reagent and the amount of product it allows.
Express and calculate concentration as molarity and related terms.

topics.title: Discovery of Sub-atomic Particles

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the properties of cathode rays and how they established the electron.
Use Thomson's e/m ratio and Millikan's charge to obtain the mass of the electron.
Recall how protons and neutrons were discovered and their properties.

topics.title: Atomic Models, Atomic Number and Isotopes

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the Thomson and Rutherford models and interpret the alpha-scattering results.
Calculate protons, neutrons and electrons from atomic number and mass number.
Distinguish isotopes from isobars.

topics.title: Wave and Particle Nature of Electromagnetic Radiation

concepts.learning_objective: Relate frequency, wavelength and wavenumber of electromagnetic radiation.
Apply Planck's quantum theory to the photoelectric effect.

topics.title: Bohr's Model for Hydrogen Atom

concepts.learning_objective: State Bohr's postulates, including quantised angular momentum and energy.
Calculate energies and wavelengths of transitions in the hydrogen atom.
Identify the limitations of Bohr's model.

topics.title: Towards Quantum Mechanical Model: Dual Behaviour and Uncertainty

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the de Broglie relation to microscopic and macroscopic particles.
Explain Heisenberg's uncertainty principle and its consequences.

topics.title: Orbitals, Quantum Numbers and Shapes of Orbitals

concepts.learning_objective: Assign allowed values of n, l, ml and ms to electrons in orbitals.
Determine the number of radial and angular nodes of orbitals.

topics.title: Energies of Orbitals and Electronic Configuration

concepts.learning_objective: Order orbital energies using the (n + l) rule and the aufbau principle.
State and apply the Pauli exclusion principle and Hund's rule.
Explain the extra stability of half-filled and completely filled subshells.

chapters.title: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

topics.title: Need for classification and genesis of periodic classification

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Dobereiner's triads and Newlands' law of octaves and state their limitations.
Explain Mendeleev's periodic law, his placement of elements and his predictions of undiscovered elements.

topics.title: Modern periodic law and the present form of the Periodic Table

concepts.learning_objective: State the modern periodic law and explain why atomic number replaced atomic mass as its basis.
Describe the periods and groups of the long form of the Periodic Table and the number of elements in each period.

topics.title: Nomenclature of elements with atomic numbers greater than 100

concepts.learning_objective: Derive the IUPAC temporary name and symbol of an element from its atomic number.
Explain why IUPAC uses temporary names and how permanent names are given.

topics.title: Electronic configurations of elements and the Periodic Table

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the number of elements in a period to the orbitals filled in that period.
Recognise that elements of a group share the same valence shell configuration.

topics.title: s-, p-, d- and f-block elements; metals, non-metals and metalloids

concepts.learning_objective: Classify elements into s-, p-, d- and f-blocks from their outer electronic configurations and locate them in the table.
Distinguish metals, non-metals and metalloids and predict trends in metallic character.

topics.title: Periodic trends in atomic and ionic radii

concepts.learning_objective: Define covalent and metallic radius and explain the trends in atomic radius across a period and down a group.
Compare the sizes of ions with their parent atoms and of isoelectronic species.

topics.title: Ionization enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy and electronegativity

concepts.learning_objective: Define ionization enthalpy and explain its periodic trends and exceptions.
Define electron gain enthalpy and explain its trends, including the exceptions of O and F.
Describe electronegativity, the Pauling scale and its periodic trends.

topics.title: Periodic trends in chemical properties and chemical reactivity

concepts.learning_objective: Predict valence, formulas of compounds and oxidation states from the position of elements.
Explain the anomalous behaviour of second period elements and the diagonal relationship.
Relate chemical reactivity across a period to the acidic, basic, amphoteric or neutral nature of oxides.

topics.title: Kossel-Lewis approach, octet rule, Lewis structures and formal charge

concepts.learning_objective: Represent valence electrons with Lewis symbols and apply the octet rule to simple molecules.
Calculate the formal charge on atoms in a Lewis structure and use it to judge structures.
Identify incomplete octets, odd-electron molecules and expanded octets as exceptions to the octet rule.

topics.title: Ionic or electrovalent bond and lattice enthalpy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the conditions that favour the formation of an ionic bond.
Define lattice enthalpy and explain its role in the stability of ionic solids.

topics.title: Bond parameters: bond length, bond angle, bond enthalpy, bond order, resonance and polarity

concepts.learning_objective: Define bond length, covalent radius, bond angle and bond enthalpy and use them in simple calculations.
Determine bond order and explain resonance using resonance structures.
Relate bond polarity and molecular geometry to the dipole moment of a molecule.

topics.title: The VSEPR theory and shapes of molecules

concepts.learning_objective: State the postulates of VSEPR theory and the order of electron-pair repulsions.
Predict shapes and bond angles of molecules whose central atom has lone pairs.

topics.title: Valence bond theory, orbital overlap and sigma and pi bonds

concepts.learning_objective: Describe covalent bond formation in H2 in terms of potential energy and orbital overlap.
Distinguish sigma and pi bonds by the type of overlap and count them in molecules.

topics.title: Hybridisation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify sp, sp2 and sp3 hybridisation and relate it to shape and s-character.
Explain sp3d and sp3d2 hybridisation in molecules such as PCl5 and SF6.

topics.title: Molecular orbital theory and bonding in homonuclear diatomic molecules

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the formation of bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals by LCAO and the conditions for combination.
Use molecular orbital configurations to find bond order, stability and magnetic nature.

topics.title: Hydrogen bonding

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the cause of hydrogen bond formation and its effect on physical properties.
Distinguish intermolecular and intramolecular hydrogen bonds with examples.

topics.title: Thermodynamic terms: system, state and internal energy

concepts.learning_objective: Classify a system as open, closed or isolated from its exchange of energy and matter.
Distinguish state functions from path-dependent quantities such as heat and work.
Apply the first law, delta U = q + w, with the IUPAC sign convention.

topics.title: Applications: work, enthalpy and heat capacity

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate pressure-volume work for expansion against a constant external pressure and for free expansion.
Relate delta H and delta U through delta H = delta U + delta n(g) RT.
Distinguish extensive and intensive properties and use heat capacities, including Cp - Cv = R.

topics.title: Measurement of delta U and delta H: calorimetry

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a bomb calorimeter measures delta U and calculate it from a temperature rise.
Explain that heat measured at constant pressure equals delta H and relate delta H to delta U for combustion.

topics.title: Enthalpy change of a reaction and Hess's law

concepts.learning_objective: Identify formation reactions and calculate reaction enthalpy from standard enthalpies of formation.
Interpret enthalpies of fusion and vaporisation and use them in enthalpy calculations.
Apply Hess's law by adding, reversing and scaling thermochemical equations.

topics.title: Enthalpies for different types of reactions

concepts.learning_objective: Use bond and atomization enthalpies to estimate reaction enthalpies for gaseous reactions.
Define lattice enthalpy and calculate it from a Born-Haber cycle.
Relate enthalpy of solution to lattice enthalpy and enthalpy of hydration.

topics.title: Spontaneity: entropy and Gibbs energy

concepts.learning_objective: Use the entropy criterion of spontaneity and calculate the entropy change of the surroundings.
Predict spontaneity from delta G = delta H - T delta S and the effect of temperature.
State the third law of thermodynamics and its use for absolute entropies.

topics.title: Gibbs energy change and equilibrium

concepts.learning_objective: State that delta r G = 0 at equilibrium and distinguish delta r G from the standard value.
Use delta r G standard = -2.303 RT log K to relate standard Gibbs energy and the equilibrium constant.

topics.title: Equilibrium in Physical Processes

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the dynamic nature of solid-liquid and liquid-vapour equilibria.
Relate equilibrium vapour pressure to the nature of a liquid and to temperature.
Apply Henry's law to equilibria involving dissolution of gases in liquids.

topics.title: Equilibrium in Chemical Processes and the Law of Chemical Equilibrium

concepts.learning_objective: Describe chemical equilibrium as dynamic and attainable from either direction.
Write Kc expressions and relate Kc values for reactions written differently.

topics.title: Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Equilibria

concepts.learning_objective: Use Kp = Kc(RT)^delta-n for gaseous equilibria.
Write equilibrium constants for heterogeneous systems omitting pure solids and liquids.

topics.title: Applications of Equilibrium Constants and Relation with Gibbs Energy

concepts.learning_objective: Predict the extent of a reaction from the magnitude of K.
Predict the direction of a reaction by comparing Qc with Kc.
Use the relation delta-G standard = -RT ln K.

topics.title: Factors Affecting Equilibria

concepts.learning_objective: Apply Le Chatelier's principle to changes in concentration and pressure.
Predict how temperature changes K for exothermic and endothermic reactions.
Explain why a catalyst and an inert gas at constant volume do not shift equilibrium.

topics.title: Acids, Bases and Their Ionization

concepts.learning_objective: Identify Arrhenius, Bronsted-Lowry and Lewis acids and bases.
Calculate pH using the ionic product of water.
Calculate the degree of ionization and pH of weak acids.

topics.title: Hydrolysis of Salts and Buffer Solutions

concepts.learning_objective: Predict the pH of salt solutions from hydrolysis of their ions.
Describe buffers and calculate their pH with the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation.

topics.title: Solubility Equilibria of Sparingly Soluble Salts

concepts.learning_objective: Relate Ksp to molar solubility and predict precipitation.
Explain and calculate the common ion effect on solubility.
